title: Excessive disclosure by parent during registration
description: The parent is asked to provide a broad set of personal data at registration, including email, full name, government ID, password, and a six-digit code. Sharing government ID at this stage may disclose more personal data than is necessary for basic account creation, increasing privacy risk at the moment of submission.
assumptions: Assumes government ID is not strictly necessary for initial registration or could be deferred or replaced with a less intrusive verification method.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives applicable threat types/positions but not detailed node ids.

title: Identification through registration data in transit
description: The flow carries directly identifying attributes such as full name, email address, and government ID. If the transmission is observable or insufficiently protected, these data can identify the parent.
assumptions: Assumes there is some possibility of interception, logging, or exposure of data in transit or associated transport metadata.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Linkability of registration events and identifiers in transit
description: The combination of email, name, government ID, and six-digit code in one registration flow can enable linking this event to the same individual across sessions, systems, or datasets if the flow or its metadata are observed.
assumptions: Assumes network metadata, repeated submissions, or shared identifiers can be correlated by an observer or intermediary.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Disclosure of sensitive credentials and identity data in transit
description: The flow includes a password and government ID, both highly sensitive. If transmitted without strong protection, intercepted, cached, or logged along the path, these data could be exposed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes transport, intermediary, or endpoint logging protections may be imperfect.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Over-collection and retention of registration data by the authentication service
description: Upon receipt, the authentication service may store or further process more personal data than necessary for authentication, especially government ID and full name, creating unnecessary disclosure and retention risk.
assumptions: Assumes the service stores or reuses all submitted fields rather than minimizing, segregating, or promptly deleting unnecessary attributes.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because detailed node mappings were not provided.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent for sensitive registration attributes
description: The authentication service may collect sensitive attributes such as government ID without clearly informing the parent why each field is needed, how long it will be retained, or with whom it will be shared, undermining awareness and consent.
assumptions: Assumes the registration interface or backend process does not provide adequate notice, purpose specification, or consent choices for these fields.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Unawareness of downstream processing of registration data
description: After receiving the registration data, the authentication service may use it for identity verification, fraud checks, analytics, or sharing with third parties without the parent being adequately aware of those downstream uses.
assumptions: Assumes downstream processing extends beyond what a parent would reasonably expect from basic authentication.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Repudiation disputes around submission of registration details
description: If the authentication service lacks privacy-preserving evidence of what was submitted and when, the parent may later dispute having provided certain attributes such as government ID or consent-related information, creating accountability and privacy issues.
assumptions: Assumes the system needs evidence of submission while also avoiding excessive logging of sensitive values.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether proof of submission and consent records are in scope for this flow; node id is approximate.

This creates an avoidable disclosure to the datastore because the act of persisting the record expands who/what can access the data and how long it exists.

title: Excessive disclosure of parent profile data in authentication response
description: The authentication service sends a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If the returned user data contains more attributes than are necessary for sign-in/session establishment (for example full profile, child-related details, internal identifiers, or account metadata), the source process causes unnecessary disclosure of personal data.

description: If the JWT itself contains personal data or sensitive claims in cleartext payload form, the authentication service discloses those attributes to the parent user device and to anyone who later gains access to the token. JWTs are often only signed, not encrypted, so included claims may be readily readable.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains readable personal claims rather than only opaque/session identifiers.
uncertainty_note: JWT contents are unspecified; threat applies when personal data is placed directly in token claims.

title: Identity disclosure via authentication response in transit
description: The flow carries a JWT and user data from the authentication service to the parent user. If transport protection is absent, weak, or terminated in an untrusted context, an observer of the flow could identify the parent user from the transmitted data or token claims.
assumptions: Assumes the channel could be observed by an attacker due to missing/weak TLS, interception on the client side, or exposure in intermediary infrastructure.
uncertainty_note: If strong end-to-end transport protection is consistently enforced, this threat is substantially reduced.

title: Linkability through stable identifiers or token claims in transit
description: Stable account identifiers, subject claims, device-correlated metadata, or repeated token structures on this flow may allow an observer or intermediary to link multiple authentication events to the same parent user across sessions.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT or accompanying user data contains stable identifiers, or that metadata such as timing/size is observable across repeated logins.
uncertainty_note: Applies most clearly when stable identifiers are exposed or metadata is available to a party observing multiple sessions.

title: Disclosure from insecure storage or handling of JWT and user data on the parent side
description: Once received, the parent user's environment may store the JWT and returned user data in browser storage, app storage, logs, screenshots, or backups. Insecure handling at the destination can expose personal data and session artifacts to other apps, local attackers, or shared-device users.
assumptions: Assumes the external entity represents a client device/application environment where storage and local processing may be insecure or shared.
uncertainty_note: This is a destination-side privacy threat contingent on client implementation and device context, which are not specified.

title: Insufficient transparency about personal data returned after authentication
description: The parent user may not be adequately informed which personal data fields are returned alongside the JWT, for what purposes they are used, and how long they are retained on the client side. This creates an unawareness threat at the destination interaction point.

title: Authentication response may violate data minimization or purpose-limitation expectations
description: Returning both a JWT and user data to the parent may exceed what is necessary for the authentication purpose if the same objective could be achieved with fewer attributes or by fetching profile data separately under clearer purpose boundaries. This can create non-compliance with privacy requirements such as data minimization and purpose limitation.
